extracted.intended_audience: journalism students and practicing sports reporters (newspaper sportswriters)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluative criteria for writing and analyzing newspaper sports game reports (box score, narrative, and post-game analysis), with attention to play description, statistics, team/individual assessment, rules, and atmosphere. Intended as a model/exemplar of sports journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spirit and determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Through sheer spirit, through indomitable determination, through utter willingness to give the final measure of physical sacrifice, those men ... lifted ... a blue banner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate teams not only on technical execution but on intangible qualities — spirit, determination, and willingness to sacrifice. The writer should note how these qualities affect the significance of a victory beyond mere statistics and describe moments that reveal them (e.g., last-minute stands, crowd reaction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Punting and drop-kicking / special teams
rubrics_metrics.description: Where Yale shone ... is in her punting and drop-kicking, her down field ability ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess special-teams play (punting, drop-kicks) and their strategic impact. Report average gains, field-position changes from punts, and any successful place/drop kicks. Use these elements to explain how a team controls territory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Close following of the ball and tackling
rubrics_metrics.description: the close, unerring following of the ball and the splendid spirit of the players individually, and as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on fundamentals: pursuit, tackling technique, and support. Specific examples (plays where tacklers held or returned kicks) help substantiate claims about defensive cohesion and tackling quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forward-passing game effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Her forward-passing game is not dangerous ... Yale's forward-passing game ... appeared to bewilder and dazzle the Tiger line ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate both the presence and effectiveness of the forward-pass: how often it is used, yards gained, whether it threatens the defense, and whether it complements the running game. Contrast attempts with their yardage and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-gain plays / off-tackle slashes
rubrics_metrics.description: She lacks long-gain plays. Perhaps she can work up her off-tackle slashes so that they will carry farther ... Nassau's off-tackle plays and delayed passes gained a great deal of ground ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess a team's ability to produce explosive plays (off-tackle runs, end-runs, delayed passes). Note frequency and success of such plays and whether the team has dependable long-gain threats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defensive formations and arrangement adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Yale's basket formation for forward-pass defence, four men back, was well conceived — it was patterned after the Harvard defence— but her normal defensive arrangement of backs, three abreast, twelve yards back, is open to grave criticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique defensive alignment and formation choices relative to opponent tactics. Describe formations used (named shifts) and explain strengths/weaknesses; explain whether the formation successfully countered opponent strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coaching, generalship and play selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Click's generalship was execrable upon many occasions ... instead of going outside tackle, Princeton essayed a series of centre bucks ... thus the downs were exhausted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess coaching decisions and overall game management: play-calling, tendency to repeat ineffective plays, use of substitutions, and tactical adjustments. Give concrete examples where coaching choice directly affected outcomes (e.g., choosing centre bucks vs outside runs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Player execution and manual errors
rubrics_metrics.description: In both, failures came through manual errors on the part of individuals ... Moore's lateral glanced from his fingers ... Dickerman's toss might have been better done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report on execution: fumbles, dropped catches, poor punts, bad throws. Distinguish errors of technique from strategic flaws and show how individual mistakes influenced the game result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discipline, penalties and undue roughness
rubrics_metrics.description: Penalties were numerous ... Yale losing 80 yards in eight setbacks to Princeton's 60 in seven infringements ... Princeton was justly penalized for undue roughness ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record and interpret penalties (type, yards lost, timing). Note incidents of roughness and their effect on momentum or scoring opportunities. Use penalties to explain swings in field position or scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical measures for team evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: The statistics of play bear out the superiority of the Yale team. Yale gained 298 yards by rushing to Princeton's 145 and made 15 first downs to the Tigers' 11. Yale essayed seven forward passes to Princeton's 10, gaining 69 yards to Princeton's 0. Yale punted 27 times to Princeton's 40 and showed an average gain of close to four yards ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include key statistics: rushing yards, passing yards, first downs, forward-pass attempts and yards gained, punts and average, penalty yards, fumbles (lost/recovered), and substitutions/number of players used. Use stats to support claims about dominance or weakness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box score essentials and scoring summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Score, Harvard 13, Penn State 13. Touchdowns, C Coolidge, Willcox, Clark. Goals from touchdowns, Withington, Lamb. Goals from field. Lamb 2. Referee, W. N. Morne of Penn. Umpire, Fred W. Murphy of Brown. Head linesman, G.V. Brown of Boston A.A. Time, 30-minute halves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise box score including final score, scoring plays (touchdowns, goals, field goals), player scoring credits, officials, and game timing. Present lineups and basic batting/field stats where applicable (baseball example shown).

rubrics_metrics.name: Play-by-play narrative detail
rubrics_metrics.description: The contest opened with an exchange of punts ... Wilson took his center's pass and ... passed the ball back to Le Gore ... Ainsworth ... ran more than 20 yards for a touchdown ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrate key sequences clearly and chronologically: who had the ball, the plays run, yardage, and outcomes. Use specific names, distances, and decisive moments to recreate the flow for readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atmosphere, crowd and contextual color
rubrics_metrics.description: From their seats the undergraduates stormed on to the field, gyrating in their uncontained exuberance, cheering, shouting ... the enormous throng standing spellbound ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe crowd behavior, setting, weather, and emotional tone to give readers a sense of occasion. Use atmosphere to underline the game's significance (university spirit, celebratory acts, solemnity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate identification of players
rubrics_metrics.description: As to the Yale players individually it is impossible to speak, because not being numbered, the various men were identified only by word of mouth and word of mouth is usually inaccurate and misleading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure accurate player identification (use jersey numbers and positions). Avoid speculation based on hearsay; if identification is uncertain, state that clearly rather than risk error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of direct quotes to illustrate mindset
rubrics_metrics.description: "I don't know that we can hold Princeton," said a Yale coach ... "Privately, I don't think we can. But you may count upon this: not a man of Yale will yield to-day until he is carried from the field."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate coach and player quotes to illuminate expectations, morale, or strategy. Use quotes to humanize analysis and to support narrative claims about resolve or outlook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative and contextual analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The wide open attack ... appeared to bewilder and dazzle the Tiger line just as much as the crimson's close formation and concealed ball offense. ... The contest had not the technical excellence of some big games we have seen — from this standpoint the Harvard-Princeton game was superior — but in its spectacular characteristics ... it stood out by itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare the match to other games, past performances, or rival teams to contextualize quality. Discuss technical excellence versus spectacle and how this game measured against benchmarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness in attributing responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: In no way can Rush be charged with the loss of either game. In both, failures came through manual errors on the part of individuals, and these no coach can prevent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance criticism between coaches and players. When assigning blame, distinguish controllable coaching mistakes from individual execution errors and avoid over-attributing responsibility without evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge and reporting of rules and rule infractions
rubrics_metrics.description: The ball was thrown away by a forward pass over the goal line, the same being translated automatically into a touchback for Yale. ... Brown ... committed the gross and inexcusable error of speaking to Capt. Glick before reporting to the referee. The referee promptly and justly set Princeton back fifteen yards ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand and explain game rules when they affect outcomes (touchback on forward pass over goal line, penalties for procedural violations). Report rule infractions and their direct impact (yardage, changed scoring opportunities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlighting individual performances and stars
rubrics_metrics.description: For Yale, Le Gore and Scovil were the stars from an offensive standpoint ... Quarterback Wilson handled his team cleverly and selected plays with splendid judgment. ... Capt Ballin was, as usual, a tower of strength.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Call out standout performers, describe their contributions (specific plays, yardage, decisions), and contrast with opponents. Use examples and stats to justify 'star' labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of technical terms and formation names with explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: She launches a driving attack from her Minnesota shift formation ... Yale's basket formation for forward-pass defence, four men back ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When mentioning technical formations or shifts (e.g., Minnesota shift, basket formation), explain briefly what they are or what effect they have so general readers can appreciate tactical points.
